h1: The 7 Best Printers for Windows 11 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Windows 11: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 printers for Windows 11, scored on driver support, document feeders and connectivity, from Brother and Canon to Epson and HP.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best printer for Windows 11: a compact mono laser with a full driver, duplex and scan tools. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the budget pick with a feeder, and the Epson ET-2800 wins on cost per page. Document-heavy offices should step up to the Epson ET-4800 for its feeder and Ethernet.
intro: Windows 11 will install a driver for nearly any printer the moment you plug it in, and that convenience is a trap. The generic driver prints a page, but it quietly hides the scan utility, the quality profiles and the maintenance tools that make a printer worth owning. Most "my printer is useless" complaints trace back to that stripped-down install, not to the hardware itself.

This ranking asks what each machine brings to a Windows 11 PC once the maker's full driver package is on it: scanning software, a feeder if you handle paperwork, wired or wireless networking and honest running costs. We reviewed seven current models and ranked them on the Primea framework, giving the most weight to everyday usability and long-term cost.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact laser with a full Windows 11 driver, scan tools, duplex and wireless.
products.description:
The Brother DCP-L2640DW is a monochrome laser with automatic duplex and wireless connectivity, backed by a full Windows 11 driver package that includes scan and maintenance tools. Laser toner does not dry out the way inkjet ink does, so a machine like this survives weeks of idle time and still prints on the first try. That matters on a home desk where printing is irregular.

It ranks above the Canon TR4720 because toner economics and a durable compact body beat cheap hardware for text work. The Canon wins on color and feeder, but its cartridge ink costs more per page.

Buy it for contracts, invoices and school documents. The caveat is firm: it prints black and white only, with no photo output, so skip it the first time a color chart is required.
products.idealFor: Home offices printing mostly text documents.
products.skipIf: You need colour or photo prints.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Colour all-in-one with an auto document feeder, fax and Canon's full Windows driver.
products.description:
Canon's PIXMA TR4720 is a color all-in-one that adds an automatic document feeder, fax and wireless printing under the full Canon Windows 11 driver. Feeders are rare at this price, and they turn scanning a 10-page form from a flatbed chore into a one-button job.

It takes second place because the feeder and low entry price are hard to match. The Epson ET-2800 prints far cheaper per page but has no feeder, and the Brother DCP-L2640DW has cheaper toner but no color. The Canon sits between them on usefulness.

Students and small offices that scan paperwork should buy it. The caveat is ink: cartridge refills cost more per page, and with no Ethernet port you depend on Wi-Fi, so heavy printers should look higher.
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page
products.idealFor: Students and small offices that scan paperwork.
products.skipIf: You print a lot and want the lowest page cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: Refillable ink tanks and the Epson Scan 2 utility for regular Windows 11 printing.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 uses refillable ink tanks, ships with startup ink bottles, and pairs with the Epson Scan 2 utility under Windows 11. Tank printing flips the usual inkjet model: you pay more up front, then refill from low-cost bottles instead of buying cartridges.

It ranks third because its flatbed scanner has no document feeder, which caps its usefulness for paperwork. Against the ET-4800 below, it costs less and does everything a home printer needs, except stack scanning and wired networking.

Buy it for steady color printing at home, where lower cost per page compounds across years. The caveat is the missing Ethernet port and feeder: multi-page scanning is slow, and a shared-office setup will outgrow it quickly.
products.idealFor: Regular colour printing on a budget over time.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One with ADF and Ethernet
products.verdict: Feeder, Ethernet and fax on top of a tank system. Stable for shared Windows 11 PCs.
products.description:
Epson's EcoTank ET-4800 adds an automatic document feeder, Ethernet and fax on top of the refillable tank system, all under the full Epson Windows 11 driver. A wired link prevents the offline errors that plague Wi-Fi printers when a router changes or the printer wakes from sleep.

It ranks fourth, not higher, because it costs more than the ET-2800 and takes more desk space, which most single-PC homes will not use. The Canon TR4720 offers a feeder for less money, but without Ethernet or tank economics.

Choose it for a shared office or a paperwork-heavy desk where several PCs print and scan stacks daily. The caveat is size and price: an occasional home printer is overpaying for the feeder and fax.

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: Colour inkjet with automatic duplex and Brother's full Windows 11 driver.
products.description:
The Brother Work Smart 1360 is a color inkjet all-in-one with automatic duplex, a 1.8 inch color display and a full Brother Windows 11 driver. Duplex on an inkjet is the feature that long-document users miss most, because it halves paper handling for reports and school packets.

It sits fifth because it has no document feeder and uses cartridges, so its running costs trail the EcoTank models above. A Refresh Subscription ink trial comes in the box, but that is a billing plan to read carefully, not a feature.

It suits a home user printing long color documents. The caveat is scanning: with a flatbed only, anyone who digitizes paperwork regularly should choose the Canon TR4720 or Epson ET-4800 instead.
products.idealFor: Home users printing long colour documents.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: HP Smart app setup and monitoring, with a 3-month Instant Ink trial included.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 is built around the HP Smart app, which handles setup, monitoring and mobile scanning, and it prints wirelessly with a flatbed scanner and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. For someone who wants to be printing in ten minutes, the guided app setup is its real selling point.

It ranks sixth because simplicity is the whole story. There is no feeder, no duplex listed in the guide and no tank economics, so it trails the Canon TR4720 in the same price bucket for anything beyond occasional pages.

Buy it for light home printing where ease matters more than cost per page. The caveat is the Instant Ink trial: it is a subscription that can bill after the trial ends, so skip it if you want to avoid recurring charges.
cons: Instant Ink trial is a subscription
products.idealFor: Light home printing with easy setup.
products.skipIf: You want to avoid ink subscriptions.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS5320 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Five individual ink tanks and Canon's full Windows 11 driver in a compact body.
products.description:
Canon's PIXMA TS5320 uses five individual ink tanks, so you replace only the color that runs out, and it works with the full Canon Windows 11 driver in a compact all-in-one body. Separate tanks avoid the waste of three-color cartridges, where one empty channel forces a whole swap.

It closes the ranking because it has a flatbed with no feeder and is an older design. It beats the HP DeskJet 4355 on ink handling, but the Canon TR4720 gives you a feeder and fax for less money.

Photo-leaning homes with small desks should pick it. The caveat is paperwork: anyone scanning multi-page documents will be doing it one sheet at a time.

whatMatters.detail: The full driver is the maker's complete software package, as opposed to the basic driver Windows 11 installs on its own. The basic one prints but often hides scanning, quality settings and maintenance tools. Download the full package from the maker's support page after setup, and check the listing for a full driver mention before you order.

Wireless is convenient but can show an offline state when a printer sleeps or the router changes. Ethernet stays steadier when several PCs print to one machine. If more than two computers will share it, look for an Ethernet port in the specs; of these picks, only the Epson ET-4800 has one.

A flatbed scanner handles one page at a time, while an automatic document feeder scans a stack unattended. If you digitize contracts, tax forms or school paperwork, a feeder saves real time. Look for ADF in the title or bullets. The Canon TR4720 and Epson ET-4800 have one; the ET-2800 and TS5320 do not.

Tank printers cost more up front but much less per page, while cartridge printers are cheap to buy and expensive to run. Estimate your monthly pages first. Light, text-only use points to a laser such as the Brother DCP-L2640DW; steady color printing points to an EcoTank. Check the ink type and the stated yield in the listing title and bullets.

Some listings include a manufacturer ink subscription trial, such as HP's Instant Ink or Brother's Refresh. These are optional plans that can start billing after the trial ends. Read the terms before enrolling and note whether the printer works normally without the plan. Look for those names in the listing bullets, the setup guide or the fine print near the ink description.

faq.q: Does Windows 11 install printer drivers automatically?
faq.a: Only a basic driver, which prints but hides scan tools and maintenance utilities. Download the full package from the maker for the Brother DCP-L2640DW, Canon PIXMA TR4720 or Epson ET-2800. That is where scanning, quality settings and cleaning tools live.

faq.q: Why does my printer show offline in Windows 11?
faq.a: Usual causes are a sleeping printer, a changed Wi-Fi network or a stuck print queue. Run the Windows printer troubleshooter first. Moving to a wired connection, like the Epson ET-4800's Ethernet port, removes most of the wireless causes.

faq.q: Is the Brother DCP-L2640DW worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: For mostly black text, yes. Toner does not dry out, so the Brother DCP-L2640DW survives long idle stretches and keeps a low cost per page. For color documents or photos, move to the Epson ET-2800 or Canon TS5320.

faq.q: Do I need a document feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan stacks of paper. The Canon TR4720 and Epson ET-4800 include feeders. For single pages and the occasional receipt, a flatbed like the Epson ET-2800 or HP DeskJet 4355 does the job fine.

faq.q: Should I accept the Instant Ink or Refresh trial?
faq.a: Only after reading the terms. The HP DeskJet 4355 includes a 3-month Instant Ink trial and the Brother Work Smart 1360 includes a Refresh trial; both can bill afterward. Skip them if you want to avoid recurring charges.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone to these?
faq.a: Yes. The HP DeskJet 4355 uses the HP Smart app for mobile scanning and printing, and the other picks offer printing from phones through the maker's own apps. Check the maker's app before buying if phone printing is a priority.

finalTake: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the right default for a Windows 11 home office that prints mostly text. Pick the Canon PIXMA TR4720 if you scan paperwork on a budget, the Epson ET-2800 for cheap color, and the ET-4800 for shared desks. Whatever you buy, install the maker's full driver, not the basic one Windows offers.
